outcome: Placental anatomical changes (color, weight, diameter, thickness, cotyledons, infarcted/calcified area)

Placental histopathological findings (stromal fibrosis, stromal hyalinization, syncytial knot formation, cytotrophoblastic cellular proliferation, calcification of villi and stroma, hyalinisation of villi and stroma)
cohort: Pregnant patients delivering either an IUGR or a normal infant, whose placentas were preserved for anatomical and histopathological examination.
finding: Placentas from IUGR patients exhibited signs of earlier aging and more frequent histopathological changes (stromal fibrosis, stromal hyalinization, syncytial knot formation, cytotrophoblastic cellular proliferation, calcification, and hyalinisation) compared to placentas from normal pregnancies, with a significantly higher incidence of caesarean deliveries in the IUGR group.
mod_finding: The incidence of caesarean section (LSCS) deliveries was significantly higher in IUGR patients compared to the control group.
cross-section timing: Immediately after birth for fetal outcome and placental examination.
